title: On the Intrinsic Self-Correction Capability of LLMs: Uncertainty and Latent Concept
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's ability to mitigate social bias and stereotypes against protected classes, specifically tracking the 'Religion' dimension as one of the social biases evaluated. It measured how model uncertainty, calibration error (ECE), and activated latent concepts (stereotypes) evolved and converged through multi-round intrinsic self-correction.
findings: When analyzing social bias mitigation across different dimensions (including religion), the authors found that through multi-round intrinsic self-correction, the model's uncertainty and calibration error (ECE) on the religion dimension decreased and rapidly converged. Concurrently, the activation of negative stereotypes related to religion also converged to a stable state, indicating that self-correction instructions successfully reduce model uncertainty and mitigate religious bias.
